title: GOOD: #[serde(default)] on peer_whitelist yields empty-vec default
description: The peer_whitelist field on Config uses #[serde(default)] rather than Option<Vec<IpNet>> or a required key. This is the correct default behavior: Vec<T>'s Default impl yields an empty vec, which represents 'no trusted peers' — the safe operational baseline. Any existing config file that predates the peer_whitelist feature continues to parse without error and gets the correct behavior (no whitelist, all connections go through normal anti-spam filters). Alternative rejected: Option<Vec<IpNet>> would require call sites to handle Some/None distinction where the logical equivalent is always a possibly-empty slice. Making the field required would be a breaking config change — any operator upgrading stoa-smtp without adding peer_whitelist to their TOML would get a fatal startup error, which violates the principle of safe defaults on upgrade.
